newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London finished higher in subdued trade. March closed $2.10 higher at $299.70 per tonne, while May added $1.30 to close at $299.20. There was no fresh news to influence prices. In New York raw sugar futures closed firmer and just below the day's highs on speculative and some trade short-covering. There was also some light buying in the March/May spread. However, physical demand remains slack, which will keep prices under pressure.

In Asia, the Thai campaign has gathered steam with 19 out of 46 registered mills now in operation after an initial delay in the northeast in November. So far the amount of crushed cane and the yield are down from the same period last year because of the delay but overall production is expected to be up on last year. Thai sugar premiums dropped further from last week due to lack of demand. Premiums for raw sugar for January/March delivery were quoted at 0.60/0.80 cents (bid/offer) over New York futures, down from around 0.80/0.90 cents last week. March/May and May/July deliveries were quoted at around 0.40/0.50 cents over New York, down from 0.45/0.55 cents for both, last week.

EU - The EU Commission has marginally reduced its beet sugar production forecast for 1996/97 to 15.580 million tonnes, white value, down from 15.593 million tonnes previously and last year's output of 15.636 million tonnes. C- quota exports were revised down to 1.583 million tonnes from 1.596 million tonnes previously and last year's figure of 1.636 million tonnes. The estimate for sugar consumption has been left unchanged at 12.6 million tonnes down from 12.65 million tonnes the previous year.

USA - The US Department of Agriculture raised its US sugar production estimate for 1996/97 (October/September) to 6.600 million tonnes, raw value, against 6.470 million tonnes forecast in November, but still down on the 6.686 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Of the total forecast for 1996/97, 3.630 million tonnes will be beet sugar and 2.976 million tonnes cane sugar. The upward revision in domestic production prompted the USDA to lower its forecast for tariff-rate quota imports to 2.260 million tonnes against 2.322 million tonnes forecast in November. All other changes in the 1996/97 balance sheet were marginal and therefore the stocks to use ratio rose to 15.6 percent against 14.7 forecast in November and the 1995/96 ratio of 15.1 percent.

DENMARK - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 3,549 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 850 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 up to 28,104 tonnes against 4,960 tonnes in 1994/95 and 8,598 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were Germany with 16,301 tonnes whites against 3,712 tonnes and Sweden with 8,442 tonnes compared to 62 tonnes. Sugar exports in September 1996 reached 13,040 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 12,827 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 up to 172,877 tonnes, down from 199,559 tonnes in 1994/95 and 255,177 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Norway with 115,528 tonnes whites against 114,082 tonnes and Sweden with 17,588 tonnes, up from 1,524 tonnes.
